output_json.patch_notes: In IOUtils.unzip: captured the extraction directory's canonical path once (destDir.getCanonicalPath()), then for every zip entry compared destFile.getCanonicalPath() against it, requiring it to equal the dir or start with dir + File.separator; otherwise an IOException("Zip slip: <entry>") is thrown before destinationParent.mkdirs() and FileOutputStream. This blocks entries like `../ESCAPED.txt` from writing outside the target. No new imports needed (File and IOException were already imported). Added IOUtilsUnzipTest with a traversal-rejection test and a normal-extraction test to prevent regressions and ensure legitimate archives still extract.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavior change is limited to rejecting archive entries that resolve outside the extraction directory; legitimate entries (including nested subdirectories) still extract normally, as verified by the second test. getCanonicalPath() can throw IOException on unusual filesystem states, but unzip already declares throws IOException, so callers are unaffected. Verified: POV now prints SAFE and exits 1 (was VULNERABLE/exit 0), module compiles, and both regression tests pass.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal (CWE-022) in com.alibaba.oneagent.utils.IOUtils.unzip. Each zip entry's resolved destination is now validated against the canonical path of the extraction directory before any parent directories are created or files are written; entries whose canonical path escapes the extraction directory throw an IOException. Added a JUnit regression test covering both the malicious traversal entry and a normal entry.
